title: Aggregate school safety can improve while some students still avoid school participation
source_unit: National Center for Education Statistics and Bureau of Justice Statistics Report on Indicators of School Crime and Safety: 2023; student School Crime Supplement and related indicators
geography: United States schools; students ages 12 to 18

observations.method: NCES/BJS compilation of national school safety indicators, including the National Crime Victimization Survey School Crime Supplement; the long-run rate and student experience measures are retained as separate indicators.
observations.uncertainty: The report is a compilation of different source surveys and years. A population rate does not identify each student's perceived safety, school response, attendance, learning, support, or later trust.
observations.subgroup: Students ages 12 to 18; the report also includes selected comparisons by school level, race/ethnicity, sex, and other characteristics.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower victimization rate may coexist with persistent fear, bullying, unequal exposure, or school-specific problems. A student may avoid school for reasons other than fear, and reported fear is not proof that an attack occurred.

observations.period: 2021-22 school year; student fear and avoidance

denominator.unit: students ages 12 to 18 enrolled in school, excluding homeschool and exclusively virtual students

afraid_at_school.unit: percent reporting sometimes or most of the time afraid of attack or harm at school

afraid_away_from_school.unit: percent reporting sometimes or most of the time afraid of attack or harm away from school

avoided_school_activities_or_classes.unit: percent avoiding school activities or classes because of fear of attack or harm

stayed_home_from_school.unit: percent staying home from school because of fear of attack or harm

observations.method: Student responses in the 2022 School Crime Supplement to the National Crime Victimization Survey, as reported in the NCES/BJS 2023 indicators report.
observations.uncertainty: Fear and avoidance are self-reported and do not identify the specific incident, person, school response, missed instruction, or later participation outcome. The measures are not a same-student longitudinal pathway.
observations.subgroup: Students ages 12 to 18; the report provides selected comparisons and separate bullying-related tables.
observations.counterinterpretation: Avoidance can be a protective choice, a short-lived response, or part of a broader attendance problem; the table does not establish harm to learning or mental health.

related_sources.claim: NCES describes the School Crime Supplement and School Survey on Crime and Safety as complementary student and principal perspectives.
BJS publication page gives the report scope and headline victimization and bullying comparisons.

boundary: This record adds a youth institutional-safety boundary: aggregate victimization, student fear, avoidance, attendance, school response, support, belonging, learning, and later trust are separate stages. It does not establish a same-student causal path or prove that aggregate safety improvement reached every student.
